title: Update a live chart by record ID
summary: Maintain a bounded window of incoming records, apply corrections, and reconcile the display after reconnecting.

identity.availability: Verified source checkout guidance; npm package, hosted site and MCP deployment identities require separate checks.

job: Show incoming observations, keep the UI stable, and correct existing records without duplicates.
dataShape: Synthetic observations with stable IDs, numeric event time and value; a four-record retained window.
fit: Use when a React application needs ref-based updates and explicit record correction.
The host owns subscription lifecycle, replay and reconnection policy.
exclusions: Static SVG cannot establish subscription cleanup, correct replay or browser lifecycle behavior.
This simulated feed is not a production network protocol, durable queue or live service.

api.name: LineChart
api.description: Line traces with curve interpolation, area fill, and point markers. Use for time series, trends, and continuous data.

xAccessor.description: Key or accessor function for x-axis values. Functions can derive a value, e.g. `d => d.timestamp`.

yAccessor.description: Key or accessor function for y-axis values. Functions support dynamic lookups, e.g. `d => d[d.metricLabel]`.

pointIdAccessor.description: Stable ID for point annotations and push-mode remove()/update().

title.description: Visible chart title and the chart's accessible name.

description.description: Concise accessible description that overrides the chart's generated aria-label.

summary.description: Screen-reader-only summary of the chart's key takeaway; include keyboard interaction guidance when relevant.

accessibleTable.description: Expose the chart data through Semiotic's screen-reader data table. Object form `{ portalTarget: string }` relocates its interactive UI to the DOM element with that ID.

portalTarget.description: ID of a DOM element outside any consumer-owned role=img wrapper. React callers may also pass an Element or a callback through the typed API.

api.schemaScope: Selected properties copied from ai/schema.json; retrieve the component resource for the full schema. React push mode follows the included behavior contracts.

contracts.title: Accessible chart text uses direct chart props
contracts.summary: High-level charts expose title for the visible name, description for a concise accessible description, summary for a screen-reader-only takeaway and interaction guidance, and accessibleTable for the data-table fallback.
contracts.action: Put title, description, summary, and accessibleTable directly on the chart component when they appear in its schema. If a consumer-owned role=img wraps the chart, use accessibleTable: { portalTarget: "element-id" } and render that target outside the image. For generated L1–L3 description or a navigable chart tree, use ChartContainer with chartConfig plus describe and/or navigable; do not invent frameProps fields.

contracts.title: Data required by usage mode
contracts.summary: Static usage (`renderChart`, MCP previews, SSR snapshots, and copy/paste examples with immediate data) requires data in props. React push mode selects live ingestion by omitting data and mutating through a ref.
contracts.action: Pass usageMode="push" to `semiotic-ai --doctor` when validating ref-based JSX with no data prop. Keep usageMode="static" or omit it for renderChart/MCP/static configs where data must be present.

contracts.title: Push mode omits data
contracts.summary: HOC push mode is selected by omitting the data prop entirely. Passing data={[]} is static empty data and can clear/reinitialize the frame on render.
contracts.action: For live charts, create a ref, omit data, then call ref.current.push() or pushMany(). For static renderChart/MCP snapshots, provide data because renderChart cannot push later.

contracts.title: Ref mutations need stable IDs
contracts.summary: push() and pushMany() can append without IDs, but remove(id) and update(id, updater) require a stable ID accessor: pointIdAccessor for XY/realtime charts, dataIdAccessor for ordinal charts, and nodeIDAccessor/edgeIdAccessor for network operations.
contracts.action: When generating code that calls remove() or update(), include the matching ID accessor and make sure pushed rows carry that ID field.

contracts.title: renderChart uses static props only
contracts.summary: MCP renderChart and semiotic/server renderChart render a single static SVG/PNG snapshot. Browser-only realtime components and future ref pushes are not renderable through that path.
contracts.action: Use renderChart only with renderable HOC components and complete static data. For live behavior, return React code with a ref and do not promise MCP-rendered output.

evidence.statement: Maintain a bounded window of incoming records, apply corrections, and reconcile the display after reconnecting.

observed.authorship: Agent-observed execution of repository tests; independent review is not recorded.

evidence.validity: Only the content digests and environment recorded here; not a release range or an adoption result.
evidence.invalidation: Changes to runtime source, schemas, manifests, task examples, tests, verification tooling or this task definition invalidate the recorded result.
expected: Corrections replace records by stable ID without increasing the retained count.
At most four records remain in the chart after new observations.
While disconnected, the displayed window remains unchanged; reconnect replaces it with the current source window.
Unmount and StrictMode cleanup leave no active subscription or playback timer.
After all five events, retained IDs obs-03 through obs-06 have values 17, 20, 16 and 19.
unassessed: Real transport failures, server retention, clock synchronization and production backpressure.
Performance on physical devices or under a production event rate.

recovery.symptom: Pushed rows disappear when React renders again.
recovery.action: Omit data entirely in push mode. Push the initial window through the mounted ref; do not pass data={[]}.
recovery.recheck: Change host UI state and confirm that the retained records survive.

recovery.symptom: A correction cannot find a record or creates duplicates.
recovery.action: Set pointIdAccessor to id and use update(id, updater). On reconnect, replace the bounded window from the authoritative host snapshot.
recovery.recheck: Inspect the chart handle's data after correction and reconnect, including IDs, values and count.

continuation.rationale: The host needs explicit correction and reconnect behavior over a bounded observation window.
recheck: Cleanup, stable IDs, retention, data-prop omission and reconnect replacement after lifecycle or dependency changes.
continuation.loss: A static export records one window. It does not carry an active subscription, prove cleanup or promise future updates.

update.previousAssumption: A static render or an empty data array demonstrates a working live chart.
update.action: Omit data for push mode. Establish the subscription after the ref mounts, correct records by ID, clean up and reconcile from the authoritative window on reconnect.
recheck: Retained records and actual canvas paint through correction, disconnect, reconnect and restart.
Subscriptions and replay timers after unmount and StrictMode cleanup.
update.remaining: Production transport reliability and event-rate performance require their own environment-specific checks.
